items.title: Dimension theory for locally algebraic k-schemes: catenarity, dimension at a point, and transcendence degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is an eleven-part collection for a locally algebraic k-scheme X: catenarity of the underlying space, dim_x(X) = dim(O_{X,x}) at closed points, invariance of the dimension under nonempty open subsets and at every point when X is irreducible, extendability of chains of irreducible closed subsets to maximal chains of length dim(X), the max-min formula for dim_x(X), dim(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) at the generic point, the drop of the transcendence degree by exactly one along an immediate specialization, dim(X) as the supremum of the transcendence degrees of generic points, the monotonicity of dim_x and dim(O_{X,x}) along specializations together with the length formula for maximal chains, the formula dim_x(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) + dim(O_{X,x}), and the increment of dim(O) by one along an immediate specialization in the irreducible or equidimensional case (statement lines 3782-3845). The author announces that instead of using the more general results proved earlier he will reduce everything to finite type k-algebras and cite the commutative algebra chapter (proof lines 3847-3851). Each part is then routed separately, mostly by replacing X by an affine neighbourhood Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra; the steps that are not formal are the reductions themselves, for instance the use of the Jacobson property of X to produce a closed point inside U cap U' in part (3) (proof lines 3876-3883), the use of the rule Z to Z cap U to compare irreducible components pointwise in part (5) (proof lines 3894-3902), and the maximal chain argument in part (7) (proof lines 3911-3918). The claim is H2: no new construction is introduced, but eleven statements each have to be routed to the correct algebra input.
